quotes: The following currency types are supported in the Braintree API. Available currencies will differ depending on your account setup and the country your company is located in.
Zero-decimal currencies are marked with an asterisk.
BGN is no longer supported for authorization or settlement. Use EUR for all transactions involving Bulgaria.
This value must be greater than 0, and must match the currency format of the merchant account.
Can only contain numbers and one decimal point (e.g. `x.xx`).
Can't be greater than the maximum allowed by the processor.
81501 Amount cannot be negative. Even if creating a credit transaction, the amount should be given as x.xx, not -x.xx.
81503 Amount is an invalid format. Amount must be formatted like '10' or '10.00'. If the currency does not use decimal places, the amount cannot include decimal places.
81528 Amount is too large. The amount cannot be greater than the maximum allowed by the processor.
81531 Amount must be greater than zero. The amount of a transaction cannot be zero.
81536 Tax amount is too large. The tax amount cannot be longer than 9 digits.
A monetary amount, either a whole number or a number with exactly two or three decimal places.

notes: The amount is a decimal string in major units: '10.00', or '10' for a zero-decimal currency. Negative amounts are an error, refunds and credits included.
Zero-decimal: the 16 ISO 0-decimal currencies listed, plus LAK (ISO 2) and ZWD (withdrawn). CLP, ISK and UGX are 0 as in ISO, unlike Adyen (CLP 2, ISK 2) and Stripe (ISK, UGX x100).
No ISO three-decimal currency (BHD, IQD, JOD, KWD, LYD, OMR, TND) is listed.
Withdrawn codes still listed: HRK, LTL, SLL, STD, ZMK (2 decimals; the page marks none of them zero-decimal) and ZWD (marked zero-decimal).
The GraphQL Amount scalar allows three decimals; the REST sale page says x.xx. toBraintree emits the currency's decimals, which both accept.

unverified.claim: Withdrawn codes HRK, LTL, SLL, STD and ZMK take 2 decimals (the page only says which currencies are zero-decimal).
Non-zero-decimal currencies take exactly their ISO 4217 decimals (the page gives no per-currency count).
Disbursements (payouts) use the same rules (no disbursement-specific amount format was found).
